cases.expected: list returns 0, 1 and 3 run branches; name prints run-<count+1>; the tree does not change

attacks.charter: Explore the run-branch count with generated repos to find a wrong n (R-047)
Explore --format with the attack corpus to find an unsafe branch name or a tree change (R-047)
attacks.input: flag-like, traversal, injection, control-chars, unicode-whitespace, format-strings, {name}/../../x, ../{name}, {name}.lock, {name}{name}, empty
attacks.observed: exit 2 JSON errors or safe names, tree unchanged

attacks.charter: Explore parse near misses to find an accidental loop kind (R-101)
Explore unicode digits and suffix lookalikes (R-101)
Explore regex characters and repeated prefix in the format (R-118)

seeds.title: branches.py name accepts negative --n
seeds.detail: name --kind run --n -5000 prints sdlc/run--5000, which parse does not read back as a run (regex needs digits only). The driver computes n from the list count, so it cannot reach this path.

seeds.title: parse treats non-ASCII digits and S-<anything> as loop kinds
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-٣ parses as run n=3 and sdlc/S-002x parses as slice. A user branch of that shape would ask for a rename or count as a run branch. The spec names only sdlc/feature-x. Python \d and a permissive slice id cause this.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline
seeds.detail: re.search with $ matches before a final newline, so sdlc/run-1<LF> parses as run. Git refuses such names, so no real branch reaches it.
